sanskrit: sa tāṃ puṣkariṇīṃ gatvā padmotpalajhaṣākulām rāmaḥ saumitrisahito vilalāpākulendriyaḥ
english: Having reached that lotus-pond teeming with blue lotuses and fish, Rāma, accompanied by Saumitri, lamented with distraught senses.

sanskrit: tasya dṛṣṭvaiva tāṃ harṣād indriyāṇi cakampire sa kāmavaśam āpannaḥ saumitrim idam abravīt
english: At the very sight of it his senses trembled with delight; overpowered by longing, he spoke thus to Saumitri.

sanskrit: saumitre paśya pampāyāḥ kānanaṃ śubhadarśanam yatra rājanti śailābhā drumāḥ saśikharā iva
english: "O Saumitri, behold the beautiful forest of Pampā, where trees that resemble mountains stand splendid, as if with crests."

sanskrit: māṃ tu śokābhisaṃtaptam ādhayaḥ pīḍayanti vai bharatasya ca duḥkhena vaidehyā haraṇena ca
english: "Yet anguishes torment me, scorched as I am by grief — by the sorrow of Bharata and by the abduction of Vaidehī."

sanskrit: adhikaṃ pravibhāty etan nīlapītaṃ tu śādvalam drumāṇāṃ vividhaiḥ puṣpaiḥ paristomair ivārpitam
english: "This meadow of blue and yellow gleams all the more richly, spread as if with garlands of the many-coloured blossoms of the trees."

sanskrit: sukhānilo 'yaṃ saumitre kālaḥ pracuramanmathaḥ gandhavān surabhir māso jātapuṣpaphaladrumaḥ
english: "O Saumitri, this season's breeze is pleasant; Kāma reigns abundantly; the month is fragrant and sweet-scented, the trees laden with flowers and fruit."

sanskrit: paśya rūpāṇi saumitre vanānāṃ puṣpaśālinām sṛjatāṃ puṣpavarṣāṇi varṣaṃ toyamucām iva
english: "See, O Saumitri, the beauty of these flower-bearing forests as they shed showers of blossoms, like rain-clouds releasing rain."

sanskrit: prastareṣu ca ramyeṣu vividhāḥ kānanadrumāḥ vāyuvegapracalitāḥ puṣpair avakiranti gām
english: "On the charming rocky ledges, diverse forest trees, shaken by the rush of the wind, scatter flowers upon the earth."

sanskrit: mārutaḥ sukhaṃ saṃsparśe vāti candanaśītalaḥ ṣaṭpadair anukūjadbhir vaneṣu madhugandhiṣu
english: "The wind blows with a pleasant touch, cool as sandalwood, in the honey-scented forests that hum with swarms of bees."

sanskrit: giriprastheṣu ramyeṣu puṣpavadbhir manoramaiḥ saṃsaktaśikharā śailā virājanti mahādrumaiḥ
english: "On the charming hillslopes, the mountains blaze with glory, their peaks interlocked with great trees full of blossoms."

sanskrit: puṣpitāgrāṃś ca paśyemān karṇikārān samantataḥ hāṭakapratisaṃchannān narān pītāmbarān iva
english: "See these karṇikāra trees in full bloom all around, covered with golden flowers — like men robed in yellow garments."

sanskrit: ayaṃ vasantaḥ saumitre nānāvihaganāditaḥ sītayā viprahīṇasya śokasaṃdīpano mama
english: "This spring, O Saumitri, resounding with many birds, fans the flames of my grief for one who is parted from Sītā."

sanskrit: māṃ hi śokasamākrāntaṃ saṃtāpayati manmathaḥ hṛṣṭaḥ pravadamānaś ca samāhvayati kokilaḥ
english: "Manmatha scorches me, overwhelmed by grief, while the joyful cuckoo calls and seems to challenge me."

sanskrit: eṣa dātyūhako hṛṣṭo ramye māṃ vananirjhare praṇadan manmathāviṣṭaṃ śocayiṣyati lakṣmaṇa
english: "This water-cock, joyful in the lovely forest waterfall, will make me grieve still more, O Lakṣmaṇa, stricken as I am with desire."

sanskrit: vimiśrā vihagāḥ pumbhir ātmavyūhābhinanditāḥ bhṛṅgarājapramuditāḥ saumitre madhurasvarāḥ
english: "Birds of mingled kinds, gladdened by their own flocking together, rejoicing with the king-bee, sing in sweet voices, O Saumitri."

sanskrit: māṃ hi sā mṛgaśāvākṣī cintāśokabalātkṛtam saṃtāpayati saumitre krūraś caitravanānilaḥ
english: "The cruel wind of Caitra's forest scorches me, O Saumitri, overwhelmed by anguished grief for that doe-eyed one."

sanskrit: śikhinībhiḥ parivṛtā mayūrā girisānuṣu manmathābhiparītasya mama manmathavardhanāḥ
english: "Peacocks attended by peahens on the mountain ridges intensify the longing of one — me — already consumed by longing."

sanskrit: paśya lakṣṇama nṛtyantaṃ mayūram upanṛtyati śikhinī manmathārtaiṣā bhartāraṃ girisānuṣu
english: "See, Lakṣmaṇa, the peacock dancing — the peahen, filled with desire, dances beside her lord on the mountain ridge."

sanskrit: mayūrasya vane nūnaṃ rakṣasā na hṛtā priyā mama tv ayaṃ vinā vāsaḥ puṣpamāse suduḥsahaḥ
english: "Surely the beloved of the peacock has not been stolen by a rākṣasa in the forest; but my dwelling without her in the month of flowers is utterly unbearable."

sanskrit: paśya lakṣmaṇa puṣpāṇi niṣphalāni bhavanti me puṣpabhārasamṛddhānāṃ vanānāṃ śiśirātyaye
english: "See, Lakṣmaṇa, the flowers become fruitless for me, even though the forests are rich with burdens of blossoms at winter's end."

sanskrit: vadanti rāvaṃ muditāḥ śakunāḥ saṃghaśaḥ kalam āhvayanta ivānyonyaṃ kāmonmādakarā mama
english: "Birds in joyful flocks cry out their melodies, calling to one another as if challenging — driving me mad with desire."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ paravaśā sītā sāpi śocaty ahaṃ yathā śyāmā padmapalāśākṣī mṛdubhāṣā ca me priyā
english: "Surely Sītā, fallen into another's power, grieves even as I do — that dark-complexioned one, lotus-petal-eyed, gentle in speech, my beloved."

sanskrit: eṣa puṣpavaho vāyuḥ sukhasparśo himāvahaḥ tāṃ vicintayataḥ kāntāṃ pāvakapratimo mama
english: "This flower-laden wind, pleasant to the touch and carrying coolness, is like fire to me as I think longingly of that beloved."

sanskrit: tāṃ vinātha vihaṃgo 'sau pakṣī praṇaditas tadā vāyasaḥ pādapagataḥ prahṛṣṭam abhinardati
english: "Without her, that bird — a crow perched in a tree — cries out joyfully, calling in its delight."

sanskrit: eṣa vai tatra vaidehyā vihagaḥ pratihārakaḥ pakṣī māṃ tu viśālākṣyāḥ samīpam upaneṣyati
english: "Surely this very bird shall be the herald of Vaidehī there; the bird will lead me to the side of the wide-eyed one."

sanskrit: paśya lakṣmaṇa saṃnādaṃ vane madavivardhanam puṣpitāgreṣu vṛkṣeṣu dvijānām upakūjatām
english: "See, Lakṣmaṇa, the chorus in the forest — heightening intoxication — of birds calling among the flower-crowned trees."

sanskrit: saumitre paśya pampāyāś citrāsu vanarājiṣu nalināni prakāśante jale taruṇasūryavat
english: "O Saumitri, see how in the variegated groves of Pampā the lotuses shine in the water like the newly-risen sun."

sanskrit: eṣā prasannasalilā padmanīlotpalāyatā haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇā pampā saugandhikāyutā
english: "Here is Pampā with her clear waters, stretching with lotuses and blue water-lilies, swarming with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks, rich with white saugandhika flowers."

sanskrit: cakravākayutā nityaṃ citraprasthavanāntarā mātaṅgamṛgayūthaiś ca śobhate salilārthibhiḥ
english: "She is ever graced with cakravāka birds, her variegated banks enclosed by groves, and she gleams with herds of elephants and deer that seek the water."

sanskrit: padmakośapalāśāni draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭir hi manyate sītāyā netrakośābhyāṃ sadṛśānīti lakṣmaṇa
english: "The eye, on beholding the petals of lotus buds, imagines they resemble the eye-cups of Sītā, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: padmakesarasaṃsṛṣṭo vṛkṣāntaraviniḥsṛtaḥ niḥśvāsa iva sītāyā vāti vāyur manoharaḥ
english: "Mingled with lotus pollen, issuing from among the trees, the enchanting breeze blows like the breath of Sītā."

sanskrit: saumitre paśya pampāyā dakṣiṇe girisānuni puṣpitāṃ karṇikārasya yaṣṭiṃ paramaśobhanām
english: "O Saumitri, see on the southern ridge of Pampā the supremely beautiful flowering stalk of the karṇikāra tree."

sanskrit: adhikaṃ śailarājo 'yaṃ dhātubhis tu vibhūṣitaḥ vicitraṃ sṛjate reṇuṃ vāyuvegavighaṭṭitam
english: "This king of mountains, adorned yet more by its mineral veins, sheds a many-coloured dust driven loose by the force of the wind."

sanskrit: giriprasthās tu saumitre sarvataḥ saṃprapuṣpitaiḥ niṣpatraiḥ sarvato ramyaiḥ pradīpā iva kuṃśukaiḥ
english: "O Saumitri, the hillslopes everywhere seem like lamps with the kiṃśuka trees in full bloom on all sides, leafless and charming."

sanskrit: pampātīraruhāś ceme saṃsaktā madhugandhinaḥ mālatīmallikāṣaṇḍāḥ karavīrāś ca puṣpitāḥ
english: "These clustered, honey-fragrant trees growing on the bank of Pampā — thickets of mālatī and mallikā — and the karavīra trees are in bloom."

sanskrit: ketakyaḥ sinduvārāś ca vāsantyaś ca supuṣpitāḥ mādhavyo gandhapūrṇāś ca kundagulmāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: "Ketakī, sinduvāra, and vāsantī are beautifully flowered; the mādhavī vines are full of fragrance, and kunda shrubs bloom everywhere."

sanskrit: ciribilvā madhūkāś ca vañjulā bakulās tathā campakās tilakāś caiva nāgavṛkṣāś ca puṣpitāḥ
english: "Ciribilvā, madhūka, vañjula, bakula, campaka, tilaka, and nāgavṛkṣa trees are all in bloom."

sanskrit: nīpāś ca varaṇāś caiva kharjūrāś ca supuṣpitāḥ aṅkolāś ca kuraṇṭāś ca cūrṇakāḥ pāribhadrakāḥ
english: "Nīpa, varaṇa, and kharjūra trees are beautifully blossoming; aṅkola, kuraṇṭa, cūrṇaka, and pāribhadraka bloom as well."

sanskrit: cūtāḥ pāṭalayaś caiva kovidārāś ca puṣpitāḥ mucukundārjunāś caiva dṛśyante girisānuṣu
english: "Mango, pāṭalā, and kovidāra trees are in flower; mucukunda and arjuna too are visible on the mountain ridges."

sanskrit: ketakoddālakāś caiva śirīṣāḥ śiṃśapā dhavāḥ śālmalyaḥ kiṃśukāś caiva raktāḥ kurabakās tathā tiniśā nakta mālāś ca candanāḥ syandanās tathā
english: "Ketaka, uddālaka, śirīṣa, śiṃśapā, dhava, śālmalī, kiṃśuka — red and blooming — kurabaka, tiniśa, naktamālā, sandal, and syandana trees as well."

sanskrit: vividhā vividhaiḥ puṣpais tair eva nagasānuṣu vikīrṇaiḥ pītaraktābhāḥ saumitre prastarāḥ kṛtāḥ
english: "The rocky ledges on the mountain ridges, O Saumitri, are made golden and red by the varied blossoms of those diverse trees scattered upon them."

sanskrit: himānte paśya saumitre vṛkṣāṇāṃ puṣpasaṃbhavam puṣpamāse hi taravaḥ saṃgharṣād iva puṣpitāḥ
english: "See, O Saumitri, the flowering of trees at winter's end; in the month of flowers the trees bloom as if through mutual friction."

sanskrit: paśya śītajalāṃ cemāṃ saumitre puṣkarāyutām cakravākānucaritāṃ kāraṇḍavaniṣevitām plavaiḥ krauñcaiś ca saṃpūrṇāṃ varāhamṛgasevitām
english: "See this cool-watered lake, O Saumitri, filled with lotuses, attended by cakravāka birds, frequented by kāraṇḍava ducks, teeming with plavas and cranes, and visited by boars and deer."

sanskrit: adhikaṃ śobhate pampāvikūjadbhir vihaṃgamaiḥ
english: "Pampā shines all the more with its calling birds."

sanskrit: dīpayantīva me kāmaṃ vividhā muditā dvijāḥ śyāmāṃ candramukhīṃ smṛtvā priyāṃ padmanibhekṣaṇām
english: "Various joyful birds seem to kindle my desire as I remember my beloved — dark-complexioned, moon-faced, lotus-eyed."

sanskrit: paya sānuṣu citreṣu mṛgībhiḥ sahitān mṛgān māṃ punar mṛgaśāvākṣyā vaidehyā virahīkṛtam
english: "See the deer accompanied by does on the variegated ridges — and me, bereft of Vaidehī of the doe-like eyes."

sanskrit: evaṃ sa vilapaṃs tatra śokopahatacetanaḥ avekṣata śivāṃ pampāṃ ramyavārivahāṃ śubhām
english: Thus lamenting there, his mind stricken by grief, he gazed upon the auspicious Pampā, her lovely waters flowing, fair and beautiful.

sanskrit: nirīkṣamāṇaḥ sahasā mahātmā sarvaṃ vanaṃ nirjharakandaraṃ ca udvignacetāḥ saha lakṣmaṇena vicārya duḥkhopahataḥ pratasthe
english: The great-souled one, gazing suddenly at the whole forest with its waterfalls and ravines, agitated of heart, deliberated together with Lakṣmaṇa, and then set forth, stricken by sorrow.

sanskrit: tāv ṛṣyamūkaṃ sahitau prayātau sugrīvaśākhāmṛgasevitaṃ tam trastās tu dṛṣṭvā harayo babhūvur mahaujasau rāghavalakṣmaṇau tau
english: Those two set forth together toward Ṛśyamūka, frequented by Sugrīva and his band of monkeys. On seeing those two — the mighty Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa — the monkeys were struck with fear.

sanskrit: tau tu dṛṣṭvā mahātmānau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau varāyudhadharau vīrau sugrīvaḥ śaṅkito 'bhavat
english: On seeing those two great-souled brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, those heroes bearing excellent weapons, Sugrīva became suspicious.

sanskrit: udvignahṛdayaḥ sarvā diśaḥ samavalokayan na vyatiṣṭhata kasmiṃś cid deśe vānarapuṃgavaḥ
english: With an anxious heart, scanning all directions, that foremost of monkeys could not stay in any one place.

sanskrit: naiva cakre manaḥ sthāne vīkṣamāṇo mahābalau kapeḥ paramabhītasya cittaṃ vyavasasāda ha
english: His mind would not settle in one spot as he watched those two of great strength; the mind of the monkey, utterly terrified, faltered.

sanskrit: cintayitvā sa dharmātmā vimṛśya gurulāghavam sugrīvaḥ paramodvignaḥ sarvair anucaraiḥ saha
english: Having pondered and weighed what was grave and what was slight, Sugrīva, greatly agitated, together with all his attendants —

sanskrit: tataḥ sa sacivebhyas tu sugrīvaḥ plavagādhipaḥ śaśaṃsa paramodvignaḥ paśyaṃs tau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: — then that lord of leaping monkeys, Sugrīva, spoke to his counsellors, utterly alarmed, watching those two — Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: etau vanam idaṃ durgaṃ vālipraṇihitau dhruvam chadmanā cīravasanau pracarantāv ihāgatau
english: "These two, surely, have been sent here by Vālin into this impenetrable forest — moving about in disguise, clad in bark garments, they have come here."

sanskrit: tataḥ sugrīvasacivā dṛṣṭvā paramadhanvinau jagmur giritaṭāt tasmād anyac chikharam uttamam
english: Then the counsellors of Sugrīva, seeing those two supreme archers, left that mountain-ledge and went to another excellent peak.

sanskrit: te kṣipram abhigamyātha yūthapā yūthaparṣabham harayo vānaraśreṣṭhaṃ parivāryopatasthire
english: Those horde-leaders quickly approached and surrounded that bull among herds, that best of monkeys, and stood in attendance.

sanskrit: ekam ekāyanagatāḥ plavamānā girer girim prakampayanto vegena girīṇāṃ śikharāṇi ca
english: Going one by one on a single path, leaping from mountain to mountain, with their speed they shook the peaks of the mountains.

sanskrit: tataḥ śākhāmṛgāḥ sarve plavamānā mahābalāḥ babhañjuś ca nagāṃs tatra puṣpitān durgasaṃśritān
english: Then all those powerful branch-animals, leaping, broke down the flowering trees that grew in those difficult places.

sanskrit: āplavanto harivarāḥ sarvatas taṃ mahāgirim mṛgamārjāraśārdūlāṃs trāsayanto yayus tadā
english: Those foremost of tawny monkeys, leaping around that great mountain on all sides, went forth frightening the deer, wildcats, and tigers.

sanskrit: tataḥ sugrīvasacivāḥ parvatendraṃ samāśritāḥ saṃgamya kapimukhyena sarve prāñjalayaḥ sthitāḥ
english: Then the counsellors of Sugrīva, having taken refuge on the king of mountains, gathered before that foremost of monkeys and all stood with hands folded in reverence.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ bhayasaṃtrastaṃ vālikilbiṣaśaṅkitam uvāca hanumān vākyaṃ sugrīvaṃ vākyakovidaḥ
english: Then Hanūmān, skilled in speech, spoke to Sugrīva who was trembling with fear and suspected the sin of Vālin.

sanskrit: yasmād udvignacetās tvaṃ pradruto haripuṃgava taṃ krūradarśanaṃ krūraṃ neha paśyāmi vālinam
english: "The one on account of whom you flee with agitated heart, O foremost of monkeys — that cruel-looking, cruel Vālin — I do not see him here."

sanskrit: yasmāt tava bhayaṃ saumya pūrvajāt pāpakarmaṇaḥ sa neha vālī duṣṭātmā na te paśyāmy ahaṃ bhayam
english: "The one from whom you fear, dear friend — your elder brother of wicked deeds — that evil-souled Vālin is not here; I see no danger for you."

sanskrit: aho śākhāmṛgatvaṃ te vyaktam eva plavaṃgama laghucittatayātmānaṃ na sthāpayasi yo matau
english: "Ah, your monkey-nature is evident indeed, O leaping one — through such fickleness of mind you cannot steady yourself in thought."

sanskrit: buddhivijñānasaṃpanna iṅgitaiḥ sarvam ācara na hy abuddhiṃ gato rājā sarvabhūtāni śāsti hi
english: "Act in everything by signs, endowed with intelligence and discernment; for a king without wisdom cannot rule all beings."

sanskrit: sugrīvas tu śubhaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvā sarvaṃ hanūmataḥ tataḥ śubhataraṃ vākyaṃ hanūmantam uvāca ha
english: Sugrīva, having heard all of Hanūmān's fair words, then spoke an even fairer speech to Hanūmān.

sanskrit: dīrghabāhū viśālākṣau śaracāpāsidhāriṇau kasya na syād bhayaṃ dṛṣṭvā etau surasutopamau
english: "Long-armed, broad-eyed, bearing arrows, bows, and swords — who would not feel fear on seeing these two who resemble sons of the gods?"

sanskrit: vālipraṇihitāv etau śaṅke 'haṃ puruṣottamau rājāno bahumitrāś ca viśvāso nātra hi kṣamaḥ
english: "I suspect these two foremost of men have been sent by Vālin; kings have many friends, and trust is not appropriate here."

sanskrit: arayaś ca manuṣyeṇa vijñeyāś channacāriṇaḥ viśvastānām aviśvastāś chidreṣu praharanti hi
english: "Enemies must be recognised by a man though they move in disguise; the untrustworthy, after gaining trust, strike at vulnerabilities."

sanskrit: kṛtyeṣu vālī medhāvī rājāno bahudarśanāḥ bhavanti parahantāras te jñeyāḥ prākṛtair naraiḥ
english: "Vālin is clever in his undertakings; kings of wide vision are destroyers of enemies — ordinary men must be alert to that."

sanskrit: tau tvayā prākṛtenaiva gatvā jñeyau plavaṃgama śaṅkitānāṃ prakāraiś ca rūpavyābhāṣaṇena ca
english: "Go to them yourself in an ordinary guise, O leaping one, and learn who they are through the means used with those who are suspected — by form and by speaking with them."

sanskrit: lakṣayasva tayor bhāvaṃ prahṛṣṭamanasau yadi viśvāsayan praśaṃsābhir iṅgitaiś ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: "Observe the disposition of those two; if their minds are joyful, reassure them again and again with praise and with signs."

sanskrit: mamaivābhimukhaṃ sthitvā pṛccha tvaṃ haripuṃgava prayojanaṃ praveśasya vanasyāsya dhanurdharau
english: "Standing in my very presence, ask them, O foremost of monkeys, what is the purpose of those bow-bearers' entry into this forest."

sanskrit: śuddhātmānau yadi tv etau jānīhi tvaṃ plavaṃgama vyābhāṣitair vā rūpair vā vijñeyā duṣṭatānayoḥ
english: "If these two have pure souls, so learn, O leaping one; their wickedness, if any, will be discerned through their speech or through their forms."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ kapirājena saṃdiṣṭo mārutātmajaḥ cakāra gamane buddhiṃ yatra tau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: Thus directed by the king of monkeys, the son of the Wind God resolved to go where those two — Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa — were.

sanskrit: tatheti saṃpūjya vacas tu tasya kapeḥ subhītasya durāsadasya mahānubhāvo hanumān yayau tadā sa yatra rāmo 'tibalaś ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Having honoured the words of that greatly fearful, unapproachable monkey with "so be it," the great-spirited Hanūmān then went to where Rāma of surpassing strength and Lakṣmaṇa were.

sanskrit: vaco vijñāya hanumān sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ parvatād ṛśyamūkāt tu pupluve yatra rāghavau
english: Hanūmān, having understood the words of the great-souled Sugrīva, leaped from the mountain Ṛśyamūka to where the two Rāghavas were.

sanskrit: sa tatra gatvā hanumān balavān vānarottamaḥ upacakrāma tau vāgbhir mṛdvībhiḥ satyavikramaḥ
english: Having gone there, the powerful Hanūmān, foremost of monkeys, of true valour, approached those two with gentle words.

sanskrit: svakaṃ rūpaṃ parityajya bhikṣurūpeṇa vānaraḥ ābabhāṣe ca tau vīrau yathāvat praśaṃsa ca
english: Abandoning his own form, the monkey approached in the guise of a mendicant and spoke to those two heroes and praised them as was fitting.

sanskrit: rājarṣidevapratimau tāpasau saṃśitavratau deśaṃ katham imaṃ prāptau bhavantau varavarṇinau
english: "You two ascetics, resembling royal sages or gods, firm in vows and of excellent complexion — how have you arrived in this place?"

sanskrit: trāsayantau mṛgagaṇān anyāṃś ca vanacāriṇaḥ pampātīraruhān vṛkṣān vīkṣamāṇau samantataḥ
english: "Frightening the herds of deer and other forest-dwellers, gazing in all directions at the trees that grow on the banks of Pampā —"

sanskrit: imāṃ nadīṃ śubhajalāṃ śobhayantau tarasvinau dhairyavantau suvarṇābhau kau yuvāṃ cīravāsasau
english: "— you who adorn this river of auspicious waters, you who are swift, steadfast, golden in lustre — who are you two, clad in bark garments?"

sanskrit: siṃhaviprekṣitau vīrau siṃhātibalavikramau śakracāpanibhe cāpe pragṛhya vipulair bhujaiḥ
english: "Heroes with the side-glance of lions, with the surpassing might and gait of lions, holding bows resembling Indra's bow in your wide arms —"

sanskrit: śrīmantau rūpasaṃpannau vṛṣabhaśreṣṭhavikramau hastihastopamabhujau dyutimantau nararṣabhau
english: "— endowed with majesty and beauty, with the gait of the foremost of bulls, with arms like an elephant's trunk, radiant, O bulls among men —"

sanskrit: prabhayā parvatendro 'yaṃ yuvayor avabhāsitaḥ rājyārhāv amaraprakhyau kathaṃ deśam ihāgatau
english: "— by whose radiance this king of mountains is illumined, you two worthy of kingship, resembling immortals — how have you come to this place?"

sanskrit: padmapatrekṣaṇau vīrau jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇau anyonyasadṛśau vīrau devalokād ivāgatau
english: "Lotus-petal-eyed heroes, wearing circles of matted locks, heroes alike to one another — you seem to have come from the world of the gods."

sanskrit: yadṛcchayeva saṃprāptau candrasūryau vasuṃdharām viśālavakṣasau vīrau mānuṣau devarūpiṇau
english: "As if by chance arrived on this earth — like the moon and the sun — broad-chested heroes, human in form but divine in appearance."

sanskrit: siṃhaskandhau mahāsattvau samadāv iva govṛṣau āyatāś ca suvṛttāś ca bāhavaḥ parighottamāḥ sarvabhūṣaṇabhūṣārhāḥ kim arthaṃ na vibhūṣitaḥ
english: "With lion shoulders, of great spirit, equal in pride like bull-oxen, your arms long and well-rounded, like the finest iron bars, worthy of all ornaments — why then are you not adorned?"

sanskrit: ubhau yogyāv ahaṃ manye rakṣituṃ pṛthivīm imām sasāgaravanāṃ kṛtsnāṃ vindhyameruvibhūṣitām
english: "I consider you both fit to protect this entire earth — with its oceans and forests, adorned with Vindhya and Meru."

sanskrit: ime ca dhanuṣī citre ślakṣṇe citrānulepane prakāśete yathendrasya vajre hemavibhūṣite
english: "And these two bows, beautiful and smooth, adorned with wondrous decorations, shine like Indra's thunderbolt decked with gold."

sanskrit: saṃpūrṇā niśitair bāṇair tūṇāś ca śubhadarśanāḥ jīvitāntakarair ghorair jvaladbhir iva pannagaiḥ
english: "And the quivers, filled with sharp arrows and fair to behold, are terrible, life-ending — like blazing serpents."

sanskrit: mahāpramāṇau vipulau taptahāṭakabhūṣitau khaḍgāv etau virājete nirmuktabhujagāv iva
english: "These two swords, of great size and broad, adorned with refined gold, blaze with glory like serpents that have shed their skins."

sanskrit: evaṃ māṃ paribhāṣantaṃ kasmād vai nābhibhāṣathaḥ
english: "Thus I address you — why do you not speak to me?"

sanskrit: sugrīvo nāma dharmātmā kaś cid vānarayūthapaḥ vīro vinikṛto bhrātrā jagad bhramati duḥkhitaḥ
english: "There is one named Sugrīva, a righteous-souled leader of a monkey troop, a hero wronged by his brother, who wanders the world in misery."

sanskrit: prāpto 'haṃ preṣitas tena sugrīveṇa mahātmanā rājñā vānaramukhyānāṃ hanumān nāma vānaraḥ
english: "I have come, sent by that great-souled Sugrīva, king among the foremost of monkeys — I am a monkey named Hanūmān."

sanskrit: yuvābhyāṃ saha dharmātmā sugrīvaḥ sakhyam icchati tasya māṃ sacivaṃ vittaṃ vānaraṃ pavanātmajam
english: "The righteous-souled Sugrīva desires friendship with you two; know me as his minister, a monkey, the son of the Wind God."

sanskrit: bhikṣurūpapraticchannaṃ sugrīvapriyakāmyayā ṛśyamūkād iha prāptaṃ kāmagaṃ kāmarūpiṇam
english: "Concealed in the guise of a mendicant, able to go wherever I will, able to take any form I wish, I have arrived here from Ṛśyamūka out of desire to please Sugrīva."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu hanumāṃs tau vīrau rāmalakṣmaṇau vākyajñau vākyakuśalaḥ punar novāca kiṃ cana
english: Having thus spoken to those two heroes, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, who were versed in speech, the one skilled in speech said nothing more.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vacas tasya rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ śrīmān bhrātaraṃ pārśvataḥ sthitam
english: Having heard his words, the glorious Rāma, with a delighted face, spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, his brother standing at his side.

sanskrit: sacivo 'yaṃ kapīndrasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ tam eva kāṅkṣamāṇasya mamāntikam upāgataḥ
english: "This is the minister of Sugrīva, the great-souled lord of monkeys, for whom I have been longing — he has come to my presence."

sanskrit: tam abhyabhāṣa saumitre sugrīvasacivaṃ kapim vākyajñaṃ madhurair vākyaiḥ snehayuktam ariṃdamam
english: "Address him, O Saumitri — this monkey who is Sugrīva's minister, versed in speech — with sweet words full of affection, O subduer of foes."
